newsitem.title: CHINA: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly down.
newsitem.headline: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly down.

text.p: Following is the China Interbank Offered Rate (CHIBOR) for Monday issued by the official Xinhua news agency on behalf of the People's Bank of China, the central bank.
The figures represent weighted averages and not closing prices and are annual percentage rates.
The central bank does not post volumes.
Traders said volume was thin today with less trade by short-term financial centres, money brokerages run by the central bank whose trading usually accounts for more than 70 percent of the market.
"Some short-term financial centres which have large funds traded less today, makin trading less active today," said one trader.
Traders said state-run commercial banks also traded less.
"Some state-owned commercial banks have strengthened control of fund mobility in the recent times with the year-end drawing near, which also helped reduce volume," said a second trader.
Traders said slow trading prevented the market rates from falling sharply though the rates were under downward pressure with the central bank expected to cut bank reserve ratios shortly.
The central bank has promised such a cut and traders believe the cut would release large amounts of short-term money into the market and help depress the rates.
But traders believe before the cut comes into effect the rates will move in a narrow range.
